Course Catalog scrape-catalog.js

Scrapes catalog.northeastern.edu — the faculty-maintained authoritative source for titles, descriptions, NUPath designations, credits, prerequisites, and corequisites. The Trigger tab card runs the script in full scrape + merge mode. The separate rotation mechanism (used by npm run data:scrape:rotate:write) scrapes one subject per run in round-robin order.

Script
scripts/scrape-catalog.js
Output
public/northeastern/catalog-courses.json
Rate limit
400 ms between requests (override: CATALOG_DELAY_MS=200)
Rotation state
data/northeastern/scrape-state.json (private) + public/northeastern/scrape-state.json (served to portal)

What the scraper extracts

For each course block on a subject page, the scraper parses:

FieldSourceNotes
title.courseblocktitleParsed from "SUBJ 1234. Title. (N Hours)"
credits / creditsMaxTitle line parentheticalVariable credits (e.g. "1–4 Hours") set both fields
description.courseblockdesc
nuPath[class*=nupath] or [class*=attribute]Text matched against NUPATH_MAP → internal codes (ND, FQ, SI, IC, EI, ER, DD, AD, WF, WD, WI, CE, EX)
prereqs.courseblockextra "Prerequisite(s):"Parsed into structured array of course refs + And/Or/( / ) tokens. Concurrent courses ("may be taken concurrently") get concurrent:true.
coreqs.courseblockextra "Corequisite(s):"List of course refs
scheduleTypeElement, number suffix, or title heuristicDefaults to "Lecture" if nothing else matches

Merge strategy

The scraper never blindly replaces the database. When merging a freshly scraped subject into catalog-courses.json:

  • Existing course: catalog fields (title, credits, description, nuPath, prereqs, coreqs) overlay the stored values. Section/term data from other sources is preserved.
  • New course (in catalog, not in our data): added.
  • Removed course (in our data, gone from catalog): kept in the file and flagged in the change log. A developer reviews via PR before deciding to delete.

Full scrape mode (Trigger tab)

The Trigger tab card runs: node scripts/scrape-catalog.js --merge --write. This fetches the subject index, scrapes every subject in sequence, merges into catalog-courses.json, and updates dataMeta.json. A complete run covers all subjects (~100+) and takes several minutes at the default 400 ms delay.

Rotation mode

For incremental updates without a full re-scrape, npm run data:scrape:rotate:write scrapes one subject per run in round-robin order. This is designed to be called frequently (e.g., as a scheduled job or CI trigger) so that all subjects are refreshed on a rolling basis.

flowchart TD A["Run: data:scrape:rotate:write"] --> B{"Subject list in\nscrape-state.json\nfresh? (<90 days)"} B -->|Yes| C["Pick subjects[nextIndex]"] B -->|No| D["Fetch subject index\nfrom catalog.northeastern.edu\nupdate listFetched"] D --> C C --> E["Scrape that subject's page\n400 ms delay between requests"] E --> F["Partial-merge into\ncatalog-courses.json"] F --> G["Advance nextIndex\n(wraps at end of list)"] G --> H["Write scrape-state.json\n+ change log entry"]

90-day subject list freshness

The rotation state stores the full list of subject URLs fetched from the catalog index (state.listFetched). If the list is empty or older than 90 days, the script re-fetches the index before picking the next subject. This handles new departments being added to the catalog without requiring a manual reset.

scrape-state.json format

{
  "nextIndex": 12,
  "subjects": [["CS", "https://catalog.northeastern.edu/course-descriptions/cs/"], ...],
  "listFetched": "2026-01-15T10:00:00.000Z",
  "lastRun": "2026-05-19T08:00:00.000Z",
  "lastScraped": { "CS": "2026-05-19T08:00:00.000Z", "EECE": "2026-05-18T08:00:00.000Z", ... }
}

Two copies are written: data/northeastern/scrape-state.json (authoritative, committed) and public/northeastern/scrape-state.json (served to the dev portal's Log tab for display).

Usage

node scripts/scrape-catalog.js                       # dry run — prints diff to stdout
node scripts/scrape-catalog.js --merge --write       # full scrape + write (Trigger tab)
node scripts/scrape-catalog.js --rotate --write      # one subject, rotate (incremental)
node scripts/scrape-catalog.js --dry-run             # first 3 subjects only (sanity check)
node scripts/scrape-catalog.js --subject CS          # single subject only
